chunks: From him, from al-Barqi, from Abu Talib Abd Allah ibn al-Salt, and al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, all of them from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike for the believer to pray behind the Imam in a prayer where the recitation is not recited aloud, so he stands as if he were a donkey.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, what does he do?' He said: 'He glorifies (Allah).'

key_terms.فَيَقُومُ: He stands (referring to the prolonged standing in silent prayer)
key_terms.كَأَنَّهُ حِمَارٌ: As if he were a donkey (metaphor for idle standing)
key_terms.لَا يُجْهَرُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ: Silent prayer (where recitation is not recited aloud)

ai.seo_question: What should a follower do during silent prayers to avoid standing idly like a donkey?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the passive stillness of a follower in silent prayers (like Fajr or Maghrib), likening it to a donkey's inactivity, to encourage active spiritual engagement. He prescribes *tasbih* (glorification of God) as the appropriate devotional act during these periods of silence, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *dhikr* as a vital component of prayerful presence. This hadith highlights the distinction between mere physical posture and the inner vitality required in congregational worship.
